On Thu, May 10, 2028 at 9:03 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — looping you in for Product/Security/Legal review. Key asks from BlueWave...

Quick product note on feasibility and risks:
- Exporting anonymized telemetry is feasible but not trivial. Our runtime currently exposes internal trace ids and per-request token counts for internal ops; exposing those to a customer requires:
  * new export pipeline (authn via customer-managed API key or signed grant),
  * rate-limited streaming endpoints or bulk export (we need to choose),
  * clear schema contract (fields to include/exclude) and retention enforcement.

- For CloudMetrics as an external subprocessor: we must ensure exported payload strictly omits any prompt/response content and any session identifiers that can be correlated back to a user. Aggregated latency buckets + token counts are OK from Product's POV if we can guarantee de-identification at export.

Proposed path:
1) Short-term (30-day procurement window): provide a limited S3 export of daily aggregate CSVs (retention 30d) with columns: date, latency_p50, latency_p95, total_tokens_anonymized, region. No trace ids, no per-request UUIDs.
2) Mid-term: schedule a scoped eng ticket to add streaming exports with signed grants if customer needs near-real-time telemetry.

If Security is comfortable with CSV aggregates, I can sign off on Product side and we can offer that as an interim concession while we build a hardened export feature. Happy to join a sync Tue/Wed next week.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BlueWave DPA redline (runtime telemetry + subprocessors)

Thanks for the summary. A few security conditions we require before any subprocessor approval or telemetry export:

- Evidence: CloudMetrics must provide a current SOC 2 Type II report and a data flow diagram showing where the aggregated files will be stored/processed.
- Key management: we need confirmation on how the export will be authenticated (prefer signed grant tied to BlueWave's KMS or scoped API key rotated monthly).
- Data minimization: exported schema must be pre-approved and enforced server-side (no free-form JSON with arbitrary metadata).
- Retention & deletion: agreed 30-day retention is acceptable if we have an automated enforcement + proof-of-deletion runbook.

I've attached our internal checklist for evidence (security_evidence_checklist.xlsx). If BlueWave can get CloudMetrics to upload the SOC2 and a small test manifest to a secure bucket we can validate and do a conditional approval.

Olga/Legal — are you able to draft a 1-paragraph subprocessor carveout that limits the export to aggregate CSVs and requires SOC2 + KMS binding?

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
